## Big idea in one line

Instead of matching every method in a package, **you mark** the methods that need the behavior:

```java
@LogExecution
public void placeOrder() { ... }
```

An aspect uses `@annotation(...)` to find those marks and run advice.  
Readable at the call site; no giant `execution` strings for every special case.

```text
custom annotation on method
        │
        ▼
@Around("@annotation(logExecution)")
        │
        ▼
timing / security / audit code
```

---

## Topic 1 — Define a custom annotation

```java
@Target(ElementType.METHOD)
@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
public @interface LogExecution {
    String value() default "";
}
```

| Meta-annotation | Why it matters |
|-----------------|----------------|
| `@Target(METHOD)` | only on methods (can also allow TYPE) |
| `@Retention(RUNTIME)` | must survive to runtime or AOP cannot see it |

Optional attributes (`value`, `level`, …) let the annotation carry config.

---

## Topic 2 — Aspect with `@annotation` binding

```java
@Aspect
@Component
public class LogExecutionAspect {

    @Around("@annotation(logExecution)")
    public Object around(ProceedingJoinPoint pjp, LogExecution logExecution) throws Throwable {
        String label = logExecution.value().isBlank()
            ? pjp.getSignature().toShortString()
            : logExecution.value();

        long start = System.currentTimeMillis();
        try {
            return pjp.proceed();
        } finally {
            System.out.println(label + " took " + (System.currentTimeMillis() - start) + "ms");
        }
    }
}
```

### Binding trick

Parameter name `logExecution` matches `@annotation(logExecution)`.  
Spring injects the annotation instance so you can read `value()`.

Alternative form:

```java
@Around("@annotation(com.example.demo.aop.LogExecution)")
public Object around(ProceedingJoinPoint pjp) throws Throwable { ... }
```

Then look up the annotation via reflection if you need attributes.

---

## Topic 3 — Use it on services

```java
@Service
public class OrderService {

    @LogExecution("place-order")
    public void placeOrder() {
        // business only
    }

    public void internalHelper() {
        // no annotation → no timing aspect
    }
}
```

**Still proxied:** the method must be called through the Spring bean/proxy.  
Self-invocation still skips the aspect (lecture 24).

---

## Topic 4 — Design patterns that fit custom annotations

| Annotation idea | Aspect behavior |
|-----------------|-----------------|
| `@LogExecution` | time + log |
| `@RequiresApiKey` | check header/security before `proceed` |
| `@Audited` | write who/when/what after success |
| `@Cacheable`-style learning demo | simple map cache around `proceed` |

Keep annotations **intention-revealing**. Business readers should understand `@Audited` without opening the aspect first.

---

## Topic 5 — Combine annotation + execution (optional)

```java
@Around("@annotation(audited) && execution(* com.example.demo.service.*.*(..))")
public Object audit(ProceedingJoinPoint pjp, Audited audited) throws Throwable {
    // ...
}
```

Useful when similar annotations might appear outside the layer you care about.

---

## Picture: annotation-driven AOP

```text
Developer puts @LogExecution on method
Spring creates proxy for the bean
Caller → proxy
          ├─ sees annotation match
          ├─ runs @Around advice
          └─ proceed() → real method
```

---

## Practice lab (IDE steps)

### Step 1 — Create `@LogExecution`

`@Target(METHOD)` + `@Retention(RUNTIME)` + optional `String value()`.

### Step 2 — Aspect

`@Around("@annotation(logExecution)")` with `ProceedingJoinPoint` + annotation param.  
Log start/end + duration.

### Step 3 — Annotate selectively

Put `@LogExecution` on two service methods only.  
Call three methods from a controller — only the annotated ones should log timing.

### Step 4 — Use the attribute

`@LogExecution("checkout")` → confirm the custom label appears in logs.

### Step 5 — Gate without proceed (mini auth annotation)

Create `@RequiresHeader` and an `@Around` that returns 401 / throws if a request header is missing.  
(Inject `HttpServletRequest` carefully via `RequestContextHolder` or pass data another way — keep the demo small.)

---

## Short map to keep

```text
Custom annotation = marker (+ optional config)
RUNTIME retention  = required
@annotation(...)   = pointcut
Bind annotation param to read attributes
Proxy rules still apply (external calls only)
```

## Exercises

1. Why is `SOURCE` retention useless for Spring AOP?  
2. How does the aspect receive the annotation’s `value()`?  
3. What happens if you annotate a private method and call it only via `this`?  
4. Name one benefit of `@LogExecution` over a wide `execution(*..service.*.*(..))`.  
5. Which starter must still be on the classpath?
